correctness.rationale: For every n>=3 and pairwise-distinct coordinate normal, the known and independently reproved product-of-simplices faces F(I,J) of the type-A root polytope meet the central hyperplane in relative interior exactly for interleaved I/J ranks. Every Q-face corresponds to exactly one such ambient face, with its dimension reduced by one; face inclusion is inherited. Each m-index union has 2^m-2m interleavings, hence f_k=binom(n,k+3)(2^(k+3)-2(k+3)). Alternating triple edges give the exact section vertices. Full proof is in RESULT.md. Exact-rational verifier passed 15 cases in n=3..7 and the 10/10/2 facet polygon spectrum in n=5; finite tests are corroboration only.

originality.rationale: The new claim concerns the entire poset of generic central hyperplane sections of complete type-A root polytopes. The strongest inspected articles determine the unsliced ambient root-polytope faces (Ardila et al.; Cellini-Marietti), describe root-polytopal subdivisions (Zhang), or address general section counts (De Loera et al. abstract only). An ambient face classification does not itself state the interleaving test, uniqueness of crossed faces, or the evaluated section f-vector; each is established here. Nearby published research results treat positive-root polytopes or other section families. An equivalent earlier derivation is a live historical-priority risk.
residual_risks: An earlier paper may express the same face-lattice or count using oriented-matroid, symmetric-edge, or coordinate-order terminology not retrieved by bounded searches.

The complete existing face lattice of the ambient type-A root polytope makes this section computation a relatively accessible corollary once the crossing lemma is applied; whether this exact corollary appeared previously remains provisional.
The 2024 general section manuscript was screened by abstract, not fully read, and is not used to certify absence of this theorem.

value.rationale: A natural infinite family of convex polytopes acquires a complete, common face lattice under every vertex-avoiding central cut. Closed formulas in all ranks and exact alternating incidence give shape-independent combinatorial topology, with cubic vertices but exponentially many facets. This is a complete natural classification with a clear question and structural content, not a one-off numeric computation; no general theorem about all polytope sections is claimed.
